answer: Reciprocal Grove Anchoring: each node must maintain a minimum number of mutually confirmed edges to distinct neighbors before its messages propagate beyond a hollow two-hop radius. Edges count only if both endpoints independently log the connection and traffic flows both ways over time. An attacker spinning up many identities must invest in sustained bidirectional traffic and persistent storage across a dune of real counterparties, since isolated clusters stay quarantined at the edge and cannot amplify. Cost: continuous bandwidth and maintenance per fake node indefinitely.
